blind_target.authors: Gould SA, Doods H, Lamla T, Pekcec A.
blind_target.title: Pharmacological characterization of intraplantar Complete Freund's Adjuvant-induced burrowing deficits.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Although burrowing is a relatively novel pain outcome measure, a few studies have reported decreased burrowing in rat models of inflammatory and neuropathic pain; importantly, burrowing deficits were reversed by known analgesics, suggesting a degree of predictive validity for this outcome measure.2,9,20,35,61,62
blind_target.outcome_quote: Overall, reduced burrowing was partially replicated at 6 of the 8 participating centres with an element of variability between and within centres.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors give an overall partial replication verdict for CFA-associated suppressed burrowing across centres.

luna_triage.reason: The multicentre study directly tests whether CFA-induced inflammation suppresses rat burrowing across new centres. Gould et al. (2016) is explicitly cited as research on intraplantar CFA-induced burrowing deficits, matching this tested finding. The supplied row is Andrews et al. (2012), a different paper on peripheral nerve injury or inflammation-associated pain; it does not represent Gould's CFA-specific report.
luna_triage.omission_quote: We hypothesise that by using a prospective multicentre design, the reliability of novel outcome measures can be efficiently and rapidly evaluated. As part of the IMI Europain collaboration (http://www.imieuropain.org), we investigated rat burrowing behaviour after induction of complete Freund adjuvant (CFA)-associated inflammation across 8 centres to assess the reliability of suppressed burrowing as a pain-related outcome measure.
